thread:
sam: Heads-up — saw a 20-40% p99 tail latency regression for streaming inference since last night's deploy. Looks host-side (tokenization/request parse) not model.
elaine: Ugh, timing? which cohort/route?
sam: Started ~03:12 UTC. Affects /v1/generate streaming and chat streaming. Canary shows more small write/syscall activity.
ben: Any traces? could be framing change or new chunker behavior.
sam: Pulled a perf trace on one host. Profiling shows syscall time dominating stacks during steady decode.
ryan: Can you paste the trace? rough numbers ok.
sam: Here's a trimmed strace-ish sample:
```
write(12, "\x00..chunk..\n", 64) = 64
write(12, "\x00..chunk..\n", 40) = 40
write(12, "\x00..chunk..\n", 32) = 32
... repeated hundreds of times per request
```
sam: Also saw many `sendmsg`/`writev` calls instead of coalesced writes. CPU time in kernel ~15-25% higher.
elaine: That smells like changed streaming chunker that flushes per token boundary. Did we flip any "flush on newline" logic?
aj: I rolled tokenization refactor yesterday to avoid head-of-line stalls in grpc parsing. Might've introduced per-token flush in host proxy.
ben: Related: KV cache miss rate doubled on those requests in the same window. Maybe chunk boundaries break prefix caching keys.
ryan: If batching heuristic sees many small frames, it may choose batch_size=1 to keep latency low, then throughput drops. Could be interacting.
sam: Experiment: toggled host proxy to use coalescing pipe (writev) and disabled the immediate flush — p99 dropped back ~25% in canary.
infra-bot: deploy-bot detected shift: host-io-syscall-spike on pool=dedicated-1 @ 1894567980
ben: We should add a micro-benchmark that simulates streaming with variable token flush frequency. Also measure kvcache hit rate per framing strategy.
aj: Reverting the tokenization refactor is painful. Alternative: change proxy coalescing at ingress to batch small writes for N ms or up to X bytes.
elaine: Agree. Need safety: ensure we don't increase latency for short requests. maybe adaptive coalescing: if request completes within T, send immediately.
ryan: Also check kernel TCP_NODELAY / Nagle interactions — if socket options differ between grpc path and http2 path, cost changes.
sam: Action items:
- aj: add microbench and test with writev vs write flush patterns (in ~2h)
- ben: profile kvcache key construction and cache hit correl w/ frame boundaries
- ryan: review ingress proxy coalescing + socket options
- elaine: help validate against canary traffic

aj: Will run perf and a small harness. I'll post numbers.
ben: I'll instrument cache metrics (per-request prefix length, frame_count).
ryan: I'll spin a quick chi-run with different socket flags.
sam: Thanks. If we confirm, we can patch proxy to coalesce small frames and revert the immediate flush, plus add a safety canary.
deploy-bot: Rolling canary rollback for service=host-proxy requested by sam @ 1894568030. Status: queued.
elaine: Also adding a note to the perf-runbook about syscall-dominated streaming cases + how to diagnose (strace snippet + perf script to look for writev/sendmsg hotspots).
sam: Yup — this was subtle: refactor improved parse latency for some large requests but regressed streaming tail due to syscall flood + kvcache thrash. Need better bench coverage. :clipboard: 
aj: Posting microbench results in a follow-up thread.
